criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The rationale and user identification are clearly articulated. However, engineering requirements and quantifiable mission goals (e.g. revisit rates, spatial resolution, payload mass/power) are lacking.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A Gantt chart and task narrative are presented, and software/links are identified. However, it lacks risk management, contingencies, or specific technical detail tying into the mission narrative.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: No actual technical engineering calculations, baseline orbit selections, or preliminary STK simulation outputs are shown. Claiming completion of introductory tutorials does not represent technical mission design progress.

evidence.quote: read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The structure and text readability are good, but the reference section consists purely of bare URLs without formal bibliographic metadata or standard citation formatting.

technical_issues.issue: Suggested leaving a satellite in-situ or boosting to a graveyard orbit without considering LEO orbital debris regulations (e.g., 25-year deorbit rule).

overall: The mission concept is well reasoned and presented. However, technical preliminary work is absent—no preliminary orbital parameters, sensor sizing, or STK outputs are included.

feedback.summary: You have articulated a compelling mission rationale and identified clear user needs for Australian marine conservation. Your document is logically structured and includes an initial project schedule. To reach higher bands, you must transition from background research to engineering execution: quantify your mission requirements, include actual preliminary orbit or sensor calculations, account for orbital debris regulations, and adopt professional bibliographic referencing.
next_steps: Define quantitative engineering requirements (such as spatial resolution, revisit time, and payload mass/power estimates) directly linked to your user needs.
Produce and document preliminary technical calculations in STK or Python, including baseline orbital parameters and coverage simulations.
Incorporate risk management, contingency buffers, and compliance with LEO orbital debris regulations (e.g., the 25-year deorbit rule) into your project plan.

criteria.C1: You clearly communicated the rationale and identified end users in 'Mission Concept & Rationale'. To reach Accomplished, define quantitative engineering requirements and measurable mission goals (such as revisit rates, spatial resolution, and payload constraints) supported by literature.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart and task narrative establish project feasibility. To achieve Accomplished, provide a robust plan that includes project variations, contingency time, and explicit risk mitigation strategies tied directly to mission challenges.
criteria.C3: Completing STK tutorials and background reading shows initial engagement, but no technical design work was presented. To reach Accomplished, include preliminary engineering results, such as baseline orbit trade-offs, coverage figures, or sensor sizing calculations.
criteria.C4: The report structure is clear and easy to read. To reach Accomplished, replace the bare URLs in 'Useful Links' with consistent, standard bibliographic citations and ensure all in-text citations follow a formal academic style.
